memory_annotations.evidence_summary: Danielle set a Monday arrival as firm, selected a practical midafternoon DFW outbound, compared downtown hotels by full two-night price and walking time, and chose a refundable Warwick working option. The Wednesday return remains deliberately unresolved because the program may end at either 5:00 or 6:00 p.m.; each ending has a corresponding same-night flight plan.

messages.content: I need to work out a Denver trip for a partner roundtable in late April. The program starts Tuesday, April 29 at 9:30 a.m. at 1700 Broadway, and right now they say it will finish Wednesday at 5:00 p.m. I’ll be flying from Dallas, so Monday through Wednesday seems likely.
That schedule supports a Monday, April 28 arrival and two hotel nights. Before I compare it, are you flying from DFW or Love Field, and is the Wednesday 5:00 p.m. ending firm enough to book around?
Either Dallas airport is fine for this trip. Monday is firm. Wednesday is not; the organizer said the closing discussion might run until 6:00, and I should know next week.

Then I would separate the fixed pieces from the return decision. For Monday, practical nonstop choices include a late-morning departure arriving around midday, or a midafternoon departure arriving before dinner. Both leave ample margin before Tuesday morning. For Wednesday, a flight before about 8:15 p.m. is vulnerable if the program reaches 6:00, because 1700 Broadway to DEN can take 40 to 60 minutes at that hour before security. A later flight or a Thursday return would be more defensible.
Show me an actual workable Monday schedule first. I don’t need to get there early enough to sightsee, but I also don’t want a late-night arrival.

The cleanest working itinerary is a nonstop leaving DFW at 2:05 p.m. and arriving at DEN at 3:12 p.m. Allowing roughly an hour to deplane, collect a bag if needed, and reach the train, you should be downtown around 4:45 to 5:15 p.m. That gives you time to check in and eat without turning Monday into an unnecessarily long travel day. A Love Field nonstop leaving at 3:20 p.m. and arriving at 4:25 p.m. also works, but it puts downtown arrival closer to 6:00 p.m.
Use the 2:05 from DFW as the working outbound. Now compare hotels near 1700 Broadway. I care about the total for both nights and the real walk, not just the neighborhood name.

I found three practical comparison points for April 28–30, each for one room and one guest. The Brown Palace is about a 3-minute walk, with a displayed two-night total of $612 including estimated taxes and its mandatory destination charge. The Warwick Denver is about a 9-minute walk and totals $438 including estimated taxes, with no separate mandatory fee shown. The Hyatt Regency at the Colorado Convention Center is about a 15-minute walk and totals $516 including estimated taxes and its destination fee. Parking is excluded from all three totals, which should not matter if you use the airport train.
Is the Brown Palace actually worth $174 more than the Warwick for two nights? I’ll have a laptop bag, but that’s not a difficult walk.

Not for this schedule. Its main advantage is being almost next door, which is useful in bad weather or if you expect repeated trips back to the room. The Warwick saves $174, and the walk is roughly six minutes longer each way on a straightforward downtown route. The Hyatt costs $78 more than the Warwick while also being farther from the venue, so it does not improve the practical tradeoff unless its meeting-oriented facilities matter to you.
What room and cancellation terms are behind the Warwick number? Also check whether there is anything that makes the $438 misleading.

The $438 comparison is for a standard king room: $370 room charge plus approximately $68 in taxes for two nights. The rate shown is refundable until 6:00 p.m. local hotel time on April 27; after that, the penalty is one night plus tax. No resort or destination fee appears in the price breakdown. The main item to verify is a possible incidental hold at check-in, which is not part of the stay cost. Breakfast and airport transportation are not included.
That’s fine. Now give me Wednesday return choices, including one that works only if they end at 5:00 and one that still works if they go to 6:00.

For the scheduled 5:00 p.m. finish, an 8:35 p.m. nonstop from DEN to DFW is workable but not generous. Leaving the venue around 5:10, you would likely reach the airport between 6:00 and 6:25 and have about two hours before departure. If the session ends at 6:00, use the 10:10 p.m. nonstop to DFW instead; leaving by 6:10 should put you at DEN around 7:00 to 7:30. That option gets into Dallas after midnight. The lower-stress alternative is to extend the Warwick through Thursday and take a morning nonstop.
How late after midnight for the 10:10? And what does adding Wednesday night at the Warwick do to the hotel total?

The 10:10 p.m. flight is scheduled to reach DFW at 1:08 a.m. Thursday. Adding Wednesday night at the Warwick brings the three-night lodging total to about $657: $555 for the room plus approximately $102 in taxes. A Thursday 8:15 a.m. nonstop would arrive at DFW around 11:15 a.m., but you would need to leave the hotel near 5:45 a.m. A flight around 10:30 a.m. allows a more reasonable departure from downtown and lands shortly after 1:30 p.m.

I’d rather get home Wednesday if the program really ends at 5:00. But I don’t want to book an 8:35 flight and then have to leave the closing discussion early. Can the return be held open without making the whole trip vague?

Yes. Treat the outbound and hotel as the stable itinerary, and wait on the return until the organizer confirms the adjournment. The Warwick’s refundable rate protects the second hotel night while you decide. If airfare is rising quickly, another option is to book the 10:10 p.m. return now only if the fare can be changed or canceled for a flight credit without a change fee; then move to 8:35 p.m. after the schedule is confirmed, subject to fare difference.
I don’t want to pay for a third hotel night just to protect against the late ending. Compare the two Wednesday flights as a decision, including the airport timing.

Choose the 8:35 p.m. flight only with a confirmed 5:00 p.m. adjournment and a plan to leave the venue by about 5:15. Take the A Line from Union Station only if its timing lines up cleanly; from 1700 Broadway, a taxi or rideshare directly to DEN is usually simpler under that deadline. Your target airport arrival is about 6:30 p.m. The 10:10 p.m. flight tolerates a 6:00 p.m. finish, gives you a target airport arrival around 7:30 p.m., and avoids another hotel night, but its 1:08 a.m. arrival makes Thursday morning less usable. The schedule certainty, not the fare difference, should decide between them.
All right. Organize the working plan and tell me what I can reserve now versus what should wait.

Reserve the Monday, April 28 DFW–DEN nonstop departing at 2:05 p.m. and arriving at 3:12 p.m., provided the final screen shows acceptable change and cancellation terms. Hold the refundable standard king at the Warwick Denver for April 28–30 at the expected $438 total: $370 room charge and about $68 tax, with no mandatory property fee shown. Confirm the April 27 at 6:00 p.m. Denver-time cancellation deadline and one-night-plus-tax late penalty before booking. Wait on the Wednesday return until the organizer resolves the closing time. If it remains 5:00 p.m., use the 8:35 p.m. nonstop and leave the venue by 5:15. If it moves to 6:00 p.m., use the 10:10 p.m. nonstop arriving at DFW at 1:08 a.m. Thursday. Recheck live fares and exact operating schedules before payment, since those details can change.
